In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.

 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

13	
14	本讲承接 u5-l1（温度采样），那里 established 的事实不再重复推导，直接使用：
15	
16	- **logits 与 softmax**：模型每步输出整个词表上的 logits，`softmax` 把它变成概率分布。
17	- **温度采样**：`scale_logits_by_temperature` 在 softmax **之前**把 logits 除以 T，T<1 锐化、T>1 平滑；采样用 `torch.multinomial`（有放回）按概率抽 token。
18	- **温度的局限**：温度只是**整体重新加权**——它把长尾概率压小，但长尾上的 token 仍然有非零概率被抽中。T 调大追求多样性时，那些概率极低的「胡言乱语」token 也会混进来；T 调小压住胡言乱语时，多样性又没了。我们想要的是「**该多样时多样、该确定时确定**」。

20	本讲需要的新概念只有三个，都很轻：
21	
22	| 概念 | 一句话解释 |
23	|---|---|
24	| **nucleus sampling（核采样 / top-p 采样）** | Holtzman 等人 2020 年提出：不固定保留「前 k 个」（top-k），而是保留**按概率从大到小排序后、累积质量首次达到 `top_p` 的最小 token 集合**（这个集合叫「核」），其余 token 概率直接置零，最后重归一化再采样。 |
25	| **累积和（cumulative sum）** | 排序后逐项往前累加。例如 `[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]` 的累积和是 `[0.5, 0.91, 1.0]`。`torch.cumsum` 一行完成。 |
26	| **熵（entropy）** | 分布「不确定性」的度量：\[ H(p) = -\sum_i p_i \ln p_i \]（单位 nat）。分布越均匀熵越大，越集中熵越小。top-p 过滤砍掉长尾后重归一化，熵必然下降——我们会在实践中亲手量出降了多少。 |
27	
28	为什么 top-p 比 top-k 更聪明？top-k 固定保留 k 个 token：面对一个很「尖」的分布（下一个词几乎确定）时，k 个还是太多，可能采出怪词；面对一个很「平」的分布（下一步真的很开放）时，k 个又太少，掐死了多样性。top-p 保留的**个数随分布形状自适应**：尖分布自动少保留，平分布自动多保留。

41	### 4.1 top_p_filter：五步流水线
42	
43	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
44	
45	`top_p_filter` 解决的问题：**在概率分布上动态划一条截止线，把长尾「核外」token 的概率清零，再把剩余质量重归一化为合法分布**，供后续 `torch.multinomial` 采样。
46	
47	它和温度的分工可以用一句话概括：
48	
49	> **温度负责「重塑」整个分布的形状，top-p 负责「砍掉」分布的尾巴。** 温度再怎么调，每个 token 的概率都还是正数；top-p 之后，核外 token 的概率严格为 0，永远不可能被采到。
50	
51	为什么要砍尾巴？实践中发现（这正是原论文标题 "The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration" 指出的现象）：语言模型分布的长尾里堆满了语料中「偶尔出现过」的低质拼接，人类文本从来不会从均匀的全词表里选词。砍掉长尾，是把采样范围收缩到「模型真正有信心的核」。
52	
53	注意函数的操作对象是**概率**（softmax 之后），不是 logits——核采样的定义就建立在「累积概率质量」上，logits 空间里没有对应物。
54	
55	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
56	
57	输入：`probas`，形状 `(batch, vocab_size)` 的概率分布（生成循环里传入的是 `(1, vocab)`，因为取了 `[:, -1]` 后仍保留 batch 维）；标量 `top_p`。
58	
59	```
60	top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
61	  0. 若 top_p 为 None 或 >= 1.0：原样返回（不过滤）
62	  1. 排序    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = 按概率降序排序（记下原位置）
63	  2. 累积和  cumprobas[j] = sorted_probas[0] + ... + sorted_probas[j]
64	  3. 选核    prefix[j] = cumprobas[j] - sorted_probas[j]   # 第 j 个 token 之前的质量
65	             keep[j]  = prefix[j] < top_p                   # 此前尚未攒够 top_p → 我属于核
66	             keep[0]  = True                                # 兜底：至少保留概率最大的 1 个
67	  4. 置零    核外 sorted_probas 置 0
68	  5. 回填    按 sorted_idx 把置零后的值散射回原始词表位置
69	  6. 重归一化 filtered / sum(filtered)，使每行重新和为 1
70	输出：与输入同形状、同「行列结构」的过滤后概率分布
71	```

77	\[
78	\begin{aligned}
79	\text{cumprobas} &= (0.5,\ 0.91,\ 1.0) \\
80	\text{prefix} &= \text{cumprobas} - p = (0,\ 0.5,\ 0.91) \\
81	\text{keep} &= \text{prefix} < 0.9 = (\text{True},\ \text{True},\ \text{False})

83	\]

89	\]

181	### 4.2 generate_text_top_p_stream_cache：温度 × top-p 组合
182	
183	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
184	
185	有了过滤器，下一步是把它接进生成循环。`generate_text_top_p_stream_cache` 就是 u5-l1 的 `generate_text_temp_stream_cache` 加了一行：在 softmax 之后、multinomial 之前插入 top-p 过滤。
186	
187	组合的直觉：
188	
189	- **温度在前（logits 层面）**：先把分布塑形——T 大则摊平（多样性），T 小则聚拢（一致性）。
190	- **top-p 在后（概率层面）**：无论温度把分布摊得多平，长尾一律清零，只从「核」里采样。
191	
192	两者搭配正是实践中最常见的配置：较高的温度提供多样性，top-p 兜底防止低质长尾 token 漏网。仓库里 `self_consistency_vote` 的默认参数就是 `temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9`（见 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L271-L272](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L271-L272)），第 5 讲的自一致性投票将直接消费这一组合。
193	
194	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
195	
196	```
197	generate_text_top_p_stream_cache(model, token_ids, max_new_tokens,
198	                                 eos_token_id, temperature=0., top_p=None):
199	  初始化：model.eval()、新建 KVCache、清零位置游标          # 与 u3-l2 相同
200	  prefill：整段 prompt 前向，取末位 logits
201	  循环 max_new_tokens 步：
202	    T=0/None → argmax（贪心；注意：top_p 完全不参与！）
203	    T>0：
204	      logits = out / temperature          # Step 3.2  温度缩放
205	      probas = softmax(logits)            # Step 3.3  概率化
206	      probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p)# Step 4    （新增）砍尾 + 重归一化
207	      next   = multinomial(probas)        # Step 3.4  采样（CPU 上执行再搬回）
208	    命中 EOS → break（EOS 不产出）
209	    yield next_token
210	    非最后一步 → 对 next_token 做 decode 前向
211	```
212	
213	顺序不可颠倒的原因：温度作用在 logits 上、top-p 定义在概率上，`softmax` 是两个世界之间唯一的桥，所以流水线只能是「缩放 logits → 概率化 → 过滤概率 → 采样」。

276	### 4.3 边界语义：`prefix < top_p` 与 `keep[:, 0] = True`
277	
278	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
279	
280	核采样的原始定义是：**保留最小的 token 集合，使其累积质量 ≥ top_p**。「最小集合」意味着：一个 token 属于核，当且仅当**在它之前的质量还没攒够 top_p**——一旦攒够了，后面的 token 就都多余了。
281	
282	源码把这句话直接翻译成了张量判据：
283	
284	\[
285	\text{keep}[j] \iff \underbrace{\sum_{i<j} p_{(i)}}_{\text{prefix}[j]} < \text{top\_p}
286	\]
287	
288	其中 \( p_{(i)} \) 是降序排列后的第 i 大概率。而 `cumprobas < top_p` 翻译的是另一句话：「连我算在内都没攒够」——它实现的是「保留质量**严格小于** top_p」，会在阈值被跨过的那一刻过早收手，丢掉跨阈值的那个 token。
289	
290	至于 `keep[:, 0] = True`：`prefix[0] = 0`，只要 `top_p > 0`，`0 < top_p` 自然成立，这一行看似多余。它的真正职责是兜住**非正的 top_p**（例如误传 `top_p=0`）：此时所有 `prefix < 0` 全为 False，若没有这行强制保留，分布会全零，重归一化除以 `clamp_min(1e-12)` 后仍全零，`multinomial` 将报「invalid distribution」错。一行兜底把「非法参数」降解为「退化为贪心」的安全行为。
291	
292	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
293	
294	三种判据在同一算例上的对比（`p = (0.5, 0.41, 0.09)`）：
295	
296	| 判据 | keep | 保留质量 | 问题 |
297	|---|---|---|---|
298	| `prefix < top_p`（源码，top_p=0.9） | (T, T, F) | **0.91 ≥ 0.9** ✓ | 无——恰好首次达到 0.9 |
299	| `cumprobas < top_p`（错误版） | (T, F, F) | 0.5 < 0.9 ✗ | 丢掉跨阈值 token，过度截断 |
300	| `cumprobas <= top_p`（另一错误版） | (T, F, F) | 0.5 < 0.9 ✗ | 本算例与 `<` 版同样过度截断；但换一组分布（如 `(0.5, 0.4, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.9`，cumprobas=(0.5, 0.9, 1.0)）它又碰巧给出 (T,T,F) 与源码一致——行为随「累积是否恰好等于 top_p」漂移，不可靠，见 4.3.5 练习 2 |
301	
302	极端 `top_p` 的行为边界：
303	
304	| top_p | 行为 | 对应源码 |
305	|---|---|---|
306	| `None` / `≥ 1.0` | 短路原样返回（恒等过滤） | L195-L196 |
307	| `0.001`（极小正数） | 核收缩到头名 token，输出退化为 one-hot `(1, 0, …, 0)`，采样等价贪心 | L207-L209 + L222 |
308	| `0` / 负数（非法） | `keep[:, 0]=True` 兜底，同样退化为 one-hot，不报错 | L209 |
309	
310	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
311	
312	**判据与兜底三行**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L204-L209](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L204-L209)）：`prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas` 用「累积和减去自身」优雅地算出「排在我之前的质量和」，避免再写一次累积；注释 "Example: [0.5, 0.41, 0.09] with top_p=0.9 should keep the first two tokens" 明确记录了边界意图——0.91 越过 0.9 的那个 token（0.41）被保留。`keep[:, 0] = True` 的注释 "(fallback for very small/non-positive top_p)" 直言其防御使命。
313	
314	**严格小于的必要性**：若写成 `prefix <= top_p`，算例 `prefix = (0, 0.5, 0.91)`、`top_p=0.9` 下结果不变（0.91 > 0.9），但在「恰好等于」的边界上（如 4.1.5 练习 1 的 `prefix[2] = 0.6`、`top_p=0.6`）会多保留一个 token。严格 `<` 让「保留质量恰好等于 top_p」时果断收手，集合真正「最小」。
315	
316	**下游对边界的依赖**：第 6 章 GRPO 的 `sample_response` 原样复用本函数（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py:L78](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py#L78)，导入见 L9）——rollout 采样同样依赖「核非空」这一兜底保证，否则一次误传参数就会让整个训练循环崩溃在 `multinomial` 上。
317	
318	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
319	
320	**实践目标**：用实验对比「正确判据」与「两种错误判据」的保留集合差异，直观理解边界含义。示例代码：
321	
322	1. **操作步骤**：
323	
324	```python
325	# 示例代码：三种判据的边界对比
326	import torch
327	from reasoning_from_scratch.ch04 import top_p_filter
328	
329	def naive_filter(probas, top_p, mode):
330	    """复刻 top_p_filter，但分别用两种可疑判据。示例代码。"""
331	    sp, si = torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)
332	    cum = torch.cumsum(sp, dim=1)
333	    if mode == "prefix":       # 源码版
334	        keep = (cum - sp) < top_p
335	    elif mode == "cum_lt":     # 错误版：< 
336	        keep = cum < top_p
337	    keep[:, 0] = True
338	    kept = torch.where(keep, sp, torch.zeros_like(sp))
339	    out = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, si, kept)
340	    return out / out.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
341	
342	cases = [
343	    ([[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]], 0.9),
344	    ([[0.5, 0.4, 0.1]],   0.6),   # 测试用例：保留质量 0.9，留前两个
345	    ([[0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1]], 0.6),  # 恰好等于边界：prefix[2]=0.6
346	]
347	for p, tp in cases:
348	    p = torch.tensor(p)
349	    ref = top_p_filter(p, top_p=tp)
350	    bad = naive_filter(p, tp, "cum_lt")
351	    kept_ref = (ref > 0).sum().item()
352	    kept_bad = (bad > 0).sum().item()
353	    print(f"top_p={tp}: 源码保留 {kept_ref} 个, 错判据保留 {kept_bad} 个")
354	```
355	
356	2. **需要观察的现象**：三个算例中错判据都比源码**少保留一个** token——丢掉的正是「跨过阈值」的那个：算例一、二里源码保留到累积质量越过 0.9/0.6 的 token，错判据在它前一位就停手；算例三里边界恰好取到精确值（`prefix[2] = 0.6` 恰等于 top_p），源码因严格 `<` 在此收手保留 2 个，错判据在 `cum[1] = 0.6` 处同样为 False，只保留 1 个。
357	3. **预期结果**：算例一：源码保留 2 个（0.5495/0.4505）、错判据保留 1 个（1.0）；算例二：源码保留 2 个（0.5556/0.4444，与 tests/test_ch04.py:L82-L91 的断言一致）、错判据保留 1 个；算例三：源码保留 2 个（0.5/0.5，保留质量恰为 0.6）、错判据保留 1 个。具体打印**待本地验证**。
358	4. 若想再探 `keep[:, 0]` 兜底，可在 `naive_filter` 里去掉那一行、传 `top_p=0.0`，观察输出全零——这就是兜底存在的理由。
359	
360	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
361	
362	**练习 1**：用一句话向同学解释 `prefix < top_p` 与 `cumprobas < top_p` 的区别。
363	
364	**答案**：前者问「**轮到我之前**质量攒够 top_p 了吗？」——没攒够我就属于核，因此恰好保留「首次达到 top_p」的最小集合；后者问「**连我算上**攒够了吗？」——会在跨过阈值前一步提前收手，保留质量严格小于 top_p，过度截断。
365	
366	**练习 2**：判据用 `cumprobas <= top_p`（把 `<` 换成 `<=`）在算例 `(0.5, 0.41, 0.09)`、`top_p=0.9` 下保留谁？在什么分布下它与源码版结果不同？
367	
368	**答案**：`cumprobas = (0.5, 0.91, 1.0)`，`<= 0.9` 给出 `(T, F, F)`，只保留头名——比源码激进。关键在于它**不稳定**：源码判据 `prefix[j] < top_p` 等价于「前一位的累积和 `cum[j-1] < top_p`」，语义在任何输入下都一致；而 `cumprobas <= top_p` 只在「某位置累积**恰好等于** top_p」时才与源码碰巧重合（如 `(0.5, 0.4, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.9`：cumprobas=(0.5, 0.9, 1.0)，`<=` 给出 (T,T,F)，恰与源码相同），其余情形照旧丢掉跨阈值 token。边界行为随输入漂移的判据无法依赖，这正是源码选择把「严格小于」放在 prefix 上的理由。数值实验见 4.3.4 算例三（`(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.6`，两版一留二、一留一）。
369	
370	**练习 3**：`denom.clamp_min(1e-12)`（L220）在什么情况下才真正派上用场？既然有 `keep[:, 0] = True`，它是不是死代码？
371	
372	**答案**：仅在「所有概率被清零」时才有意义，而 `keep[:, 0] = True` 加上 softmax 输出恒正已经排除了这种情况（分母 ≥ 最大概率 > 0），所以对本函数的合法调用而言它是防御性冗余，不是死代码——它是纵深防御的一层：将来若有人改判据、传 NaN/全零张量或复用此函数到非 softmax 输入上，clamp 把「除零崩溃」降解为「输出极端值」，配合测试更容易暴露问题而非静默炸掉。
373	
374	## 5. 综合实践
375	
376	**任务：写一个「top-p 扫描器」，量化核大小与熵随 top_p 的变化。**
377	
378	不带模型、纯 CPU 张量运算即可完成，把本讲三个模块串起来：
379	
380	1. 构造三个「性格不同」的分布（示例代码）：
381	   - 尖峰型：`[0.9, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02]`（下一词几乎确定）
382	   - 平坦型：`[0.3, 0.28, 0.25, 0.17]`（下一步很开放）
383	   - 现实型：`[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]`（本讲算例）
384	2. 对每个分布，让 `top_p` 从 0.1 扫到 1.0（步长 0.1），逐档调用 `top_p_filter`，记录三列：**保留 token 数**、**过滤前保留质量**（重归一化之前的行和）、**过滤后分布的熵**。
385	3. 把结果整理成表，回答三个问题：
386	   - 同一 `top_p` 下，尖峰型与平坦型保留的 token 数差多少？（top-p 的自适应性）
387	   - 熵随 `top_p` 下降的速度，尖峰型和平坦型哪个更陡？为什么？
388	   - `top_p=1.0` 这一档走的是哪条分支（对照 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L195-L196](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L195-L196)），熵等于多少？
389	4. **预期结果**（手算可先行推出，程序验证待本地进行）：尖峰型在 `top_p=0.9` 时只保留 1 个 token（第 2 个的 prefix=0.9 不小于 0.9，熵为 0）；平坦型在 `top_p=0.9` 时保留**全部 4 个**（第 4 个 token 的 prefix=0.83 < 0.9，仍属核，熵不变）；现实型如正文，保留 2 个、熵约 0.689 nat——三种「性格」在同一 `top_p` 下的核大小截然不同，这正是 top-p 优于固定个数 top-k 的地方。
390	
391	进阶（可选）：仿照 `count_samples`（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L132-L147](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L132-L147)）对过滤后的分布各采样 1000 次，用频率分布复算熵，验证「采样频率 ≈ 概率」在核变小后收敛更快还是更慢。
392	
393	## 6. 本讲小结
394	
395	- `top_p_filter` 是一条五步流水线：**排序 → 累积和 → 前缀质量判据选核 → 置零并回填原词表位置 → 重归一化**，作用于 softmax 之后的概率，输出仍是合法分布。
396	- 边界判据 `prefix < top_p` 精确翻译了核采样定义「累积质量首次达到 top_p 的最小集合」；写成 `cumprobas < top_p` 会丢掉跨阈值的 token，导致过度截断（算例：0.91 vs 0.5）。
397	- `keep[:, 0] = True` 是极端/非法 `top_p`（如 0 或负数）下的兜底，保证核非空，把崩溃降解为「退化为贪心」。
398	- `top_p=1.0` 或 `None` 走短路分支原样返回；极小 `top_p` 使分布坍缩为 one-hot，等价 argmax。
399	- `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache` 在温度采样三步（缩放→softmax→multinomial）中间插入过滤这一步，形成「logits 层调温、概率层砍尾」的分工；**`temperature=0` 时 top-p 完全被绕过**，这是实验中最常见的坑。

# Top-p（核采样）过滤

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. **手推** nucleus sampling（核采样）的累积概率保留集合：给定一组概率和 `top_p`，能算出哪些 token 被保留、保留质量是多少。
2. **解释**源码中 `prefix < top_p`（而不是 `cumprobas < top_p`）这一边界写法的确切含义，以及它为什么恰好实现了论文中「累积质量首次达到 top_p 的最小集合」这一定义。
3. **验证** `keep[:, 0] = True` 的最小保留兜底在极端 `top_p` 下如何避免「全零分布」这一非法输入。
4. 读懂 `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache`，说清温度缩放与 top-p 过滤在流水线中的**先后顺序**与**分工**，以及 `temperature=0` 时 top-p 会被绕过这一容易踩坑的细节。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲承接 u5-l1（温度采样），那里 established 的事实不再重复推导，直接使用：

- **logits 与 softmax**：模型每步输出整个词表上的 logits，`softmax` 把它变成概率分布。
- **温度采样**：`scale_logits_by_temperature` 在 softmax **之前**把 logits 除以 T，T<1 锐化、T>1 平滑；采样用 `torch.multinomial`（有放回）按概率抽 token。
- **温度的局限**：温度只是**整体重新加权**——它把长尾概率压小，但长尾上的 token 仍然有非零概率被抽中。T 调大追求多样性时，那些概率极低的「胡言乱语」token 也会混进来；T 调小压住胡言乱语时，多样性又没了。我们想要的是「**该多样时多样、该确定时确定**」。

本讲需要的新概念只有三个，都很轻：

| 概念 | 一句话解释 |
|---|---|
| **nucleus sampling（核采样 / top-p 采样）** | Holtzman 等人 2020 年提出：不固定保留「前 k 个」（top-k），而是保留**按概率从大到小排序后、累积质量首次达到 `top_p` 的最小 token 集合**（这个集合叫「核」），其余 token 概率直接置零，最后重归一化再采样。 |
| **累积和（cumulative sum）** | 排序后逐项往前累加。例如 `[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]` 的累积和是 `[0.5, 0.91, 1.0]`。`torch.cumsum` 一行完成。 |
| **熵（entropy）** | 分布「不确定性」的度量：\[ H(p) = -\sum_i p_i \ln p_i \]（单位 nat）。分布越均匀熵越大，越集中熵越小。top-p 过滤砍掉长尾后重归一化，熵必然下降——我们会在实践中亲手量出降了多少。 |

为什么 top-p 比 top-k 更聪明？top-k 固定保留 k 个 token：面对一个很「尖」的分布（下一个词几乎确定）时，k 个还是太多，可能采出怪词；面对一个很「平」的分布（下一步真的很开放）时，k 个又太少，掐死了多样性。top-p 保留的**个数随分布形状自适应**：尖分布自动少保留，平分布自动多保留。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

|---|---|

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 top_p_filter：五步流水线

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`top_p_filter` 解决的问题：**在概率分布上动态划一条截止线，把长尾「核外」token 的概率清零，再把剩余质量重归一化为合法分布**，供后续 `torch.multinomial` 采样。

它和温度的分工可以用一句话概括：

> **温度负责「重塑」整个分布的形状，top-p 负责「砍掉」分布的尾巴。** 温度再怎么调，每个 token 的概率都还是正数；top-p 之后，核外 token 的概率严格为 0，永远不可能被采到。

为什么要砍尾巴？实践中发现（这正是原论文标题 "The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration" 指出的现象）：语言模型分布的长尾里堆满了语料中「偶尔出现过」的低质拼接，人类文本从来不会从均匀的全词表里选词。砍掉长尾，是把采样范围收缩到「模型真正有信心的核」。

注意函数的操作对象是**概率**（softmax 之后），不是 logits——核采样的定义就建立在「累积概率质量」上，logits 空间里没有对应物。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

输入：`probas`，形状 `(batch, vocab_size)` 的概率分布（生成循环里传入的是 `(1, vocab)`，因为取了 `[:, -1]` 后仍保留 batch 维）；标量 `top_p`。

```
top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
  0. 若 top_p 为 None 或 >= 1.0：原样返回（不过滤）
  1. 排序    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = 按概率降序排序（记下原位置）
  2. 累积和  cumprobas[j] = sorted_probas[0] + ... + sorted_probas[j]
  3. 选核    prefix[j] = cumprobas[j] - sorted_probas[j]   # 第 j 个 token 之前的质量
             keep[j]  = prefix[j] < top_p                   # 此前尚未攒够 top_p → 我属于核
             keep[0]  = True                                # 兜底：至少保留概率最大的 1 个
  4. 置零    核外 sorted_probas 置 0
  5. 回填    按 sorted_idx 把置零后的值散射回原始词表位置
  6. 重归一化 filtered / sum(filtered)，使每行重新和为 1
输出：与输入同形状、同「行列结构」的过滤后概率分布
```

用规格里给定的例子手推一遍（这是本讲的核心算例，后面实践会验证）：

排序后概率 \( p = (0.5,\ 0.41,\ 0.09) \)，取 \( \text{top\_p} = 0.9 \)。

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{cumprobas} &= (0.5,\ 0.91,\ 1.0) \\
\text{prefix} &= \text{cumprobas} - p = (0,\ 0.5,\ 0.91) \\
\text{keep} &= \text{prefix} < 0.9 = (\text{True},\ \text{True},\ \text{False})
\end{aligned}
\]

保留前两个 token，保留质量 \( 0.5 + 0.41 = 0.91 \ge 0.9 \)——恰好是「累积质量**首次达到** 0.9 的最小集合」。重归一化后：

\[
\left( \frac{0.5}{0.91},\ \frac{0.41}{0.91},\ 0 \right) \approx (0.5495,\ 0.4505,\ 0)
\]

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**入口与短路分支**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L194-L196](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L194-L196)）：`top_p=None` 或 `top_p>=1.0` 时直接返回原张量——`top_p=1.0` 意味着「核 = 整个词表」，过滤是恒等操作，这一行短路既省计算又是文档（默认无过滤）。函数签名从这里也可看出它期望二维输入（下面所有操作都在 `dim=1` 即词表维上进行）。

**Step 4.1 排序**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L198-L199](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L198-L199)）：`torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)` 同时返回排好序的值 `sorted_probas` 和「排序前每个值住在哪个词表位置」的索引 `sorted_idx`。后者是第 5 步回填的钥匙——概率必须回到它原来的词表 id 上，否则采样出的 token id 会张冠李戴。

**Step 4.2 累积和**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L201-L202](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L201-L202)）：`torch.cumsum` 沿词表维做前缀和，得到每个排序位上的累积质量。

**Step 4.3.1 前缀质量判据与兜底**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L204-L209](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L204-L209)）：

```python
prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas   # cumulative mass before each token
keep = prefix < top_p
keep[:, 0] = True
```

三行是整个函数的灵魂，4.3 节专门拆解。此处先记结论：`keep[j]` 为真的条件是「排在我前面的 token 总质量还没攒够 top_p」，即「把我也算进来才凑得出 top_p」；`keep[:, 0] = True` 保证概率最高的 token 永远在核里。源码注释里给出的算例正是我们手推过的 `[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]`、`top_p=0.9` 保留前两个。

**Step 4.3.2 核外置零**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L211-L215](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L211-L215)）：`torch.where(keep, sorted_probas, 0)` 在**排序坐标系**里把核外概率清零——被清零的是「排序后第 j 大」的位置，还不是词表位置。

**Step 4.3.3 回填原顺序**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L216-L217](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L216-L217)）：

```python
filtered = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, sorted_idx, kept_sorted)
```

`scatter` 是 `gather` 的逆操作：对每个排序位 j，执行 `filtered[sorted_idx[j]] = kept_sorted[j]`，把值送回原始词表 id。排序→过滤→回填，词表位置自始至终没有丢失。

**Step 4.4 重归一化**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L219-L222](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L219-L222)）：砍尾后每行和小于 1（上例为 0.91），除以行和恢复成合法分布——`torch.multinomial` 要求输入行和为 1。`keepdim=True` 让分母保持 `(batch, 1)` 形状从而正确广播（源码注释直言这对批量情形是必要的）；`clamp_min(1e-12)` 是防御性下限，防止全零分布除零——正常路径下 `keep[:, 0] = True` 已保证分母不小于最大概率，必然大于 0。

**测试如何锁定行为**（[tests/test_ch04.py:L82-L91](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/tests/test_ch04.py#L82-L91)）：`[0.5, 0.4, 0.1]`、`top_p=0.6` 时断言输出为 `[0.5556, 0.4444, 0.0]`。手推验证：`prefix = (0, 0.5, 0.9)`，`keep = (T, T, F)`，保留质量 0.9，\( 0.5/0.9 \approx 0.5556 \)、\( 0.4/0.9 \approx 0.4444 \)，与断言一致；同测试还断言 `top_p=1.0` 时输出与输入逐位相等（走的是 L195 的短路）。第二个测试（[tests/test_ch04.py:L94-L107](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/tests/test_ch04.py#L94-L107)）用一个两行、每行分布不同的批量输入验证：各行独立排序、独立截断、独立重归一化，两行和都回到 1。

**答案**：砍尾后行和小于 1（例中为 0.91）。`torch.multinomial` 要求每行概率和为 1（带容差）；更重要的是，不归一化会把 9% 的概率质量凭空蒸发，剩余 token 的相对比例虽不变，但采样在数学上不再是合法分布，行为未定义/报错。重归一化把 0.91 的质量按原比例放大回 1，核内两个 token 的相对比例 `0.5 : 0.41` 保持不变。

### 4.2 generate_text_top_p_stream_cache：温度 × top-p 组合

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

有了过滤器，下一步是把它接进生成循环。`generate_text_top_p_stream_cache` 就是 u5-l1 的 `generate_text_temp_stream_cache` 加了一行：在 softmax 之后、multinomial 之前插入 top-p 过滤。

组合的直觉：

- **温度在前（logits 层面）**：先把分布塑形——T 大则摊平（多样性），T 小则聚拢（一致性）。
- **top-p 在后（概率层面）**：无论温度把分布摊得多平，长尾一律清零，只从「核」里采样。

两者搭配正是实践中最常见的配置：较高的温度提供多样性，top-p 兜底防止低质长尾 token 漏网。仓库里 `self_consistency_vote` 的默认参数就是 `temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9`（见 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L271-L272](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L271-L272)），第 5 讲的自一致性投票将直接消费这一组合。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```
generate_text_top_p_stream_cache(model, token_ids, max_new_tokens,
                                 eos_token_id, temperature=0., top_p=None):
  初始化：model.eval()、新建 KVCache、清零位置游标          # 与 u3-l2 相同
  prefill：整段 prompt 前向，取末位 logits
  循环 max_new_tokens 步：
    T=0/None → argmax（贪心；注意：top_p 完全不参与！）
    T>0：
      logits = out / temperature          # Step 3.2  温度缩放
      probas = softmax(logits)            # Step 3.3  概率化
      probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p)# Step 4    （新增）砍尾 + 重归一化
      next   = multinomial(probas)        # Step 3.4  采样（CPU 上执行再搬回）
    命中 EOS → break（EOS 不产出）
    yield next_token
    非最后一步 → 对 next_token 做 decode 前向
```

顺序不可颠倒的原因：温度作用在 logits 上、top-p 定义在概率上，`softmax` 是两个世界之间唯一的桥，所以流水线只能是「缩放 logits → 概率化 → 过滤概率 → 采样」。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**函数签名与默认值**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L225-L233](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L225-L233)）：与 `generate_text_temp_stream_cache` 相比只多了一个 `top_p=None` 参数。**注意默认 `temperature=0.`**——直接调用而不传温度时走贪心分支，`top_p` 形同虚设（见下）。缓存初始化（`model.eval()`、新建 `KVCache`、`reset_kv_cache()`）与 u3-l2 讲过的骨架逐行相同。

**贪心分支绕过过滤器**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L244-L245](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L244-L245)）：`temperature` 为 `None` 或 `0.0` 时直接 `argmax`。这是本函数最值得划线的细节：**top-p 只在 `temperature > 0` 时生效**。逻辑上也自洽——argmax 选出的必然是概率最大的 token，它永远在核内（`keep[:, 0] = True`），过滤与否不改变结果，干脆跳过。但做实验时若忘了设温度，会误以为 top-p「不起作用」。

**采样三步 + 新增一步**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L248-L259](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L248-L259)）：与 u5-l1 精读过的 `generate_text_temp_stream_cache`（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L174-L181](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L174-L181)）逐行对照，唯一的新增是 L255 的 `probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p)`，插在 softmax（L252）与 `multinomial`（L258）之间。采样在 CPU 上执行（`probas.cpu()`）再把结果搬回原设备——与 u3-l2/u5-l1 观察到的约定一致。`top_p=None` 时过滤器走短路分支原样返回，函数行为退化为纯温度采样——一个函数覆盖三种模式（贪心 / 纯温度 / 温度+top-p）。

**EOS 提前停止与收尾**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L261-L267](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L261-L267)）：EOS 检查在 yield 之前（EOS 本身不产出），`step + 1 < max_new_tokens` 跳过最后一次前向——均为 u3-l2 已建立的模式，不再展开。

**测试中的间接验证**（[tests/test_ch04.py:L110-L126](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/tests/test_ch04.py#L110-L126)）：虽然没有专门针对 `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache` 的测试，但温度版与 top-p 版共享同一骨架；该测试用 `DummyModelCache`（logits 恒定、argmax 必中 EOS）验证「首个 token 即 EOS → 产出为空、`eval`/`reset_kv_cache` 均被调用」，这一行为对 top-p 版同样成立。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `top_p_filter` 被放在 softmax 之后而不是之前？

**答案**：`top_p_filter` 的输入是概率——它要做累积和、与 `top_p` 比较质量、重归一化，这些操作都定义在概率单纯形上；而温度缩放作用于 logits。流水线「除以 T → softmax → 过滤 → 采样」是两种操作的天然分工：温度重塑整个分布的形状，top-p 在已成形的概率上砍尾。

**练习 2**：调用 `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache(model, ids, 20, temperature=0.0, top_p=0.1)`，top-p 起作用了吗？输出和 `generate_text_basic_stream_cache`（u3-l2）有何关系？

**答案**：没起作用。`temperature=0.0` 走 argmax 贪心分支（L244-L245），`top_p_filter` 根本不被调用。输出与贪心流式生成完全一致（逐 token 相同）——argmax 选中的 token 永远是排序后第 0 位，任何合法的 top-p 核都包含它。

**练习 3**：`self_consistency_vote` 里对同一条 prompt 采样 10 次（`temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9`），为什么每次结果可以不同？随机性来自哪一行？

**答案**：随机性来自 `torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)`（L258）：过滤后的分布仍有多个非零概率的 token（核内），multinomial 按概率抽取，每次调用独立。top-p 并不消除随机性，它只是把随机性**限制在高质量核内**——这正是自一致性投票（u5-l4）能采出「和而不同」的多条推理路径、再投票的前提。

### 4.3 边界语义：`prefix < top_p` 与 `keep[:, 0] = True`

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

核采样的原始定义是：**保留最小的 token 集合，使其累积质量 ≥ top_p**。「最小集合」意味着：一个 token 属于核，当且仅当**在它之前的质量还没攒够 top_p**——一旦攒够了，后面的 token 就都多余了。

源码把这句话直接翻译成了张量判据：

\[
\text{keep}[j] \iff \underbrace{\sum_{i<j} p_{(i)}}_{\text{prefix}[j]} < \text{top\_p}
\]

其中 \( p_{(i)} \) 是降序排列后的第 i 大概率。而 `cumprobas < top_p` 翻译的是另一句话：「连我算在内都没攒够」——它实现的是「保留质量**严格小于** top_p」，会在阈值被跨过的那一刻过早收手，丢掉跨阈值的那个 token。

至于 `keep[:, 0] = True`：`prefix[0] = 0`，只要 `top_p > 0`，`0 < top_p` 自然成立，这一行看似多余。它的真正职责是兜住**非正的 top_p**（例如误传 `top_p=0`）：此时所有 `prefix < 0` 全为 False，若没有这行强制保留，分布会全零，重归一化除以 `clamp_min(1e-12)` 后仍全零，`multinomial` 将报「invalid distribution」错。一行兜底把「非法参数」降解为「退化为贪心」的安全行为。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

三种判据在同一算例上的对比（`p = (0.5, 0.41, 0.09)`）：

| 判据 | keep | 保留质量 | 问题 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prefix < top_p`（源码，top_p=0.9） | (T, T, F) | **0.91 ≥ 0.9** ✓ | 无——恰好首次达到 0.9 |
| `cumprobas < top_p`（错误版） | (T, F, F) | 0.5 < 0.9 ✗ | 丢掉跨阈值 token，过度截断 |
| `cumprobas <= top_p`（另一错误版） | (T, F, F) | 0.5 < 0.9 ✗ | 本算例与 `<` 版同样过度截断；但换一组分布（如 `(0.5, 0.4, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.9`，cumprobas=(0.5, 0.9, 1.0)）它又碰巧给出 (T,T,F) 与源码一致——行为随「累积是否恰好等于 top_p」漂移，不可靠，见 4.3.5 练习 2 |

极端 `top_p` 的行为边界：

| top_p | 行为 | 对应源码 |
|---|---|---|
| `None` / `≥ 1.0` | 短路原样返回（恒等过滤） | L195-L196 |
| `0.001`（极小正数） | 核收缩到头名 token，输出退化为 one-hot `(1, 0, …, 0)`，采样等价贪心 | L207-L209 + L222 |
| `0` / 负数（非法） | `keep[:, 0]=True` 兜底，同样退化为 one-hot，不报错 | L209 |

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**判据与兜底三行**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L204-L209](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L204-L209)）：`prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas` 用「累积和减去自身」优雅地算出「排在我之前的质量和」，避免再写一次累积；注释 "Example: [0.5, 0.41, 0.09] with top_p=0.9 should keep the first two tokens" 明确记录了边界意图——0.91 越过 0.9 的那个 token（0.41）被保留。`keep[:, 0] = True` 的注释 "(fallback for very small/non-positive top_p)" 直言其防御使命。

**严格小于的必要性**：若写成 `prefix <= top_p`，算例 `prefix = (0, 0.5, 0.91)`、`top_p=0.9` 下结果不变（0.91 > 0.9），但在「恰好等于」的边界上（如 4.1.5 练习 1 的 `prefix[2] = 0.6`、`top_p=0.6`）会多保留一个 token。严格 `<` 让「保留质量恰好等于 top_p」时果断收手，集合真正「最小」。

**下游对边界的依赖**：第 6 章 GRPO 的 `sample_response` 原样复用本函数（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py:L78](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py#L78)，导入见 L9）——rollout 采样同样依赖「核非空」这一兜底保证，否则一次误传参数就会让整个训练循环崩溃在 `multinomial` 上。

#### 4.3.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用实验对比「正确判据」与「两种错误判据」的保留集合差异，直观理解边界含义。示例代码：

1. **操作步骤**：

```python
# 示例代码：三种判据的边界对比
import torch
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch04 import top_p_filter

def naive_filter(probas, top_p, mode):
    """复刻 top_p_filter，但分别用两种可疑判据。示例代码。"""
    sp, si = torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)
    cum = torch.cumsum(sp, dim=1)
    if mode == "prefix":       # 源码版
        keep = (cum - sp) < top_p
    elif mode == "cum_lt":     # 错误版：< 
        keep = cum < top_p
    keep[:, 0] = True
    kept = torch.where(keep, sp, torch.zeros_like(sp))
    out = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, si, kept)
    return out / out.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)

cases = [
    ([[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]], 0.9),
    ([[0.5, 0.4, 0.1]],   0.6),   # 测试用例：保留质量 0.9，留前两个
    ([[0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1]], 0.6),  # 恰好等于边界：prefix[2]=0.6
]
for p, tp in cases:
    p = torch.tensor(p)
    ref = top_p_filter(p, top_p=tp)
    bad = naive_filter(p, tp, "cum_lt")
    kept_ref = (ref > 0).sum().item()
    kept_bad = (bad > 0).sum().item()
    print(f"top_p={tp}: 源码保留 {kept_ref} 个, 错判据保留 {kept_bad} 个")
```

2. **需要观察的现象**：三个算例中错判据都比源码**少保留一个** token——丢掉的正是「跨过阈值」的那个：算例一、二里源码保留到累积质量越过 0.9/0.6 的 token，错判据在它前一位就停手；算例三里边界恰好取到精确值（`prefix[2] = 0.6` 恰等于 top_p），源码因严格 `<` 在此收手保留 2 个，错判据在 `cum[1] = 0.6` 处同样为 False，只保留 1 个。
3. **预期结果**：算例一：源码保留 2 个（0.5495/0.4505）、错判据保留 1 个（1.0）；算例二：源码保留 2 个（0.5556/0.4444，与 tests/test_ch04.py:L82-L91 的断言一致）、错判据保留 1 个；算例三：源码保留 2 个（0.5/0.5，保留质量恰为 0.6）、错判据保留 1 个。具体打印**待本地验证**。
4. 若想再探 `keep[:, 0]` 兜底，可在 `naive_filter` 里去掉那一行、传 `top_p=0.0`，观察输出全零——这就是兜底存在的理由。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：用一句话向同学解释 `prefix < top_p` 与 `cumprobas < top_p` 的区别。

**答案**：前者问「**轮到我之前**质量攒够 top_p 了吗？」——没攒够我就属于核，因此恰好保留「首次达到 top_p」的最小集合；后者问「**连我算上**攒够了吗？」——会在跨过阈值前一步提前收手，保留质量严格小于 top_p，过度截断。

**练习 2**：判据用 `cumprobas <= top_p`（把 `<` 换成 `<=`）在算例 `(0.5, 0.41, 0.09)`、`top_p=0.9` 下保留谁？在什么分布下它与源码版结果不同？

**答案**：`cumprobas = (0.5, 0.91, 1.0)`，`<= 0.9` 给出 `(T, F, F)`，只保留头名——比源码激进。关键在于它**不稳定**：源码判据 `prefix[j] < top_p` 等价于「前一位的累积和 `cum[j-1] < top_p`」，语义在任何输入下都一致；而 `cumprobas <= top_p` 只在「某位置累积**恰好等于** top_p」时才与源码碰巧重合（如 `(0.5, 0.4, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.9`：cumprobas=(0.5, 0.9, 1.0)，`<=` 给出 (T,T,F)，恰与源码相同），其余情形照旧丢掉跨阈值 token。边界行为随输入漂移的判据无法依赖，这正是源码选择把「严格小于」放在 prefix 上的理由。数值实验见 4.3.4 算例三（`(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.6`，两版一留二、一留一）。

**练习 3**：`denom.clamp_min(1e-12)`（L220）在什么情况下才真正派上用场？既然有 `keep[:, 0] = True`，它是不是死代码？

**答案**：仅在「所有概率被清零」时才有意义，而 `keep[:, 0] = True` 加上 softmax 输出恒正已经排除了这种情况（分母 ≥ 最大概率 > 0），所以对本函数的合法调用而言它是防御性冗余，不是死代码——它是纵深防御的一层：将来若有人改判据、传 NaN/全零张量或复用此函数到非 softmax 输入上，clamp 把「除零崩溃」降解为「输出极端值」，配合测试更容易暴露问题而非静默炸掉。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：写一个「top-p 扫描器」，量化核大小与熵随 top_p 的变化。**

不带模型、纯 CPU 张量运算即可完成，把本讲三个模块串起来：

1. 构造三个「性格不同」的分布（示例代码）：
   - 尖峰型：`[0.9, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02]`（下一词几乎确定）
   - 平坦型：`[0.3, 0.28, 0.25, 0.17]`（下一步很开放）
   - 现实型：`[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]`（本讲算例）
2. 对每个分布，让 `top_p` 从 0.1 扫到 1.0（步长 0.1），逐档调用 `top_p_filter`，记录三列：**保留 token 数**、**过滤前保留质量**（重归一化之前的行和）、**过滤后分布的熵**。
3. 把结果整理成表，回答三个问题：
   - 同一 `top_p` 下，尖峰型与平坦型保留的 token 数差多少？（top-p 的自适应性）
   - 熵随 `top_p` 下降的速度，尖峰型和平坦型哪个更陡？为什么？
   - `top_p=1.0` 这一档走的是哪条分支（对照 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L195-L196](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L195-L196)），熵等于多少？
4. **预期结果**（手算可先行推出，程序验证待本地进行）：尖峰型在 `top_p=0.9` 时只保留 1 个 token（第 2 个的 prefix=0.9 不小于 0.9，熵为 0）；平坦型在 `top_p=0.9` 时保留**全部 4 个**（第 4 个 token 的 prefix=0.83 < 0.9，仍属核，熵不变）；现实型如正文，保留 2 个、熵约 0.689 nat——三种「性格」在同一 `top_p` 下的核大小截然不同，这正是 top-p 优于固定个数 top-k 的地方。

进阶（可选）：仿照 `count_samples`（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L132-L147](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L132-L147)）对过滤后的分布各采样 1000 次，用频率分布复算熵，验证「采样频率 ≈ 概率」在核变小后收敛更快还是更慢。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `top_p_filter` 是一条五步流水线：**排序 → 累积和 → 前缀质量判据选核 → 置零并回填原词表位置 → 重归一化**，作用于 softmax 之后的概率，输出仍是合法分布。
- 边界判据 `prefix < top_p` 精确翻译了核采样定义「累积质量首次达到 top_p 的最小集合」；写成 `cumprobas < top_p` 会丢掉跨阈值的 token，导致过度截断（算例：0.91 vs 0.5）。
- `keep[:, 0] = True` 是极端/非法 `top_p`（如 0 或负数）下的兜底，保证核非空，把崩溃降解为「退化为贪心」。
- `top_p=1.0` 或 `None` 走短路分支原样返回；极小 `top_p` 使分布坍缩为 one-hot，等价 argmax。
- `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache` 在温度采样三步（缩放→softmax→multinomial）中间插入过滤这一步，形成「logits 层调温、概率层砍尾」的分工；**`temperature=0` 时 top-p 完全被绕过**，这是实验中最常见的坑。
- 温度 + top-p 的组合（如 0.8 + 0.9）是仓库的标准采样配置，被 `self_consistency_vote` 消费，并被第 6 章 `sample_response` 原样复用——本讲的过滤器是全书推理时扩展与 RL 训练的公共零件。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **u5-l3（思维链提示实验）**：换一个不采样的推理时扩展手段——只改提示模板、权重与采样参数都不动，对比两者「花钱买准确率」的方式有何不同。
- **u5-l4（自一致性投票）**：看 `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache`（`temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9`）采出的多条推理路径如何经 `extract_final_candidate`（u4-l2）提取短答案、再 `Counter` 投票定案——本讲的过滤器正是那里多样性与质量兼得的来源。
- **源码延伸**：提前翻一眼 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py:L78](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py#L78)，确认 GRPO 的 rollout 采样循环与本讲 L252-L258 几乎逐行同构，为单元七热身。
- **理论延伸**：读 Holtzman 等人 2020 年的 *The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration*（本书第 4 章的参考之一），看人类文本的「核质量」统计如何支撑「只在核内采样」这一设计。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
